summary: This ROS Wiki page documents rosserial, a point-to-point version of ROS communications over serial, mainly used to connect low-cost microcontrollers such as Arduino to ROS. It describes the suite's client libraries, PC-side bridge nodes (rosserial_python and rosserial_server), example tutorials, and limitations such as buffer sizes, the lack of 64-bit floats, string and array handling. It also details the packet format and topic negotiation protocol, plus per-distribution package and build status from electric through noetic.
one_line: rosserial is a ROS wiki package suite that wraps ROS messages over serial links to connect microcontrollers like Arduino to ROS.
key_facts: ROS Serial is a point-to-point version of ROS communications over serial, primarily for integrating low-cost microcontrollers (Arduino) into ROS.
rosserial consists of a general p2p protocol, libraries for use with Arduino, and nodes for the PC/Tablet side, currently in both Python and Java.
The package is maintained by Michael Ferguson and Adam Stambler and is licensed under BSD.
The number of Publishers and Subscribers for rosserial_client is limited to 25 by default, and buffer sizes are limited to 512 bytes by default.
For rosserial_arduino, the ATMEGA168 has 150/150 byte input/output buffers and 6/6 publishers/subscribers.
The ATMEGA328P has 280/280 byte input/output buffers and 25/25 publishers/subscribers.
The Arduino does not support 64-bit float datatypes, so make_library automatically converts 64-bit floats into 32-bit datatypes with possible loss of precision.
Messages larger than the buffer size are not transmitted, and a ROS error message is relayed.
Topic IDs 0-100 are reserved for system functions, as defined in the rosserial_msgs/TopicInfo message.
The packet format begins with a sync flag of 0xff, followed by a protocol version byte, message length bytes, a length checksum, a topic ID, serialized data, and a data checksum.
The protocol version byte was 0xff on ROS Groovy and 0xfe on ROS Hydro, Indigo, and Jade.
rosserial_python is described as a Python-based implementation recommended for PC usage, while rosserial_server is a C++ implementation recommended for high-performance applications.
Before data transfer, the PC/Tablet side queries the embedded device for topic names and types using topic ID 0.
The page's rosserial_arduino support covers boards including UNO, Leonardo, MEGA, DUE, Teensy 3.x and LC, Spark, STM32F1, STM32Duino, ESP8266 and ESP32.
